metadata.title: Claimed and Measured: Gyro-S v2 on Real Coding Tasks, and Why the Test Needs Testing Too
metadata.description:
A model announcement claims Gyro-S v2 drifts 18% less on held-out text, 27% less on tool calls and 14% less on code than its base. We asked what the same model does as a local coding worker - writing files that hidden tests grade - and measured it head-to-head against Signal 2 on one Apple M5 Max: 20 questions, 40 easy and 40 hard graded function tasks, and five replayed real repository fixes, each run once.

Accuracy is at best a draw: on the hard set Gyro-S v2 reaches 35/40 against Signal 2's 37/40, and the easy and short sets are similar. Speed is not: Gyro-S v2 is slower everywhere - 899-1,195 s against 490-624 s on the hard set, 2,861 s against 2,141 s on the real tasks run alone, and a much lower token rate.

Stability is where they really differ: Gyro-S v2 swings from run to run (hard 8-35/40, short 2-17/20) because it often stops early with answers missing, while Signal 2 stays inside a narrow band (hard 30-37/40). On the real tasks Gyro-S v2 tends to be weaker (3/5, 4/5, and one incomplete run an engine stall ended) against Signal 2's 4/5, 5/5, 3/5, 3/5 and 4/5 - a tendency, not a clean gap, since each ran once.

In memory, Signal 2 holds about 27 GB per instance mostly on the GPU; Gyro-S v2 keeps a smaller footprint (16-26 GB) but a far larger resident size (35-49 GB), because its experts and PLE table are read from the SSD, and two instances of it leave only about 4 GB free.

Our first run had loaded the wrong PLE table - the base model's instead of the one this model card pairs with - which made Gyro-S v2 look far worse than it is; we found that after the author's question and reran. One lesson: verify the test and the setup before a verdict.

Sixth report of the PAI Reports series. Sources: https://github.com/mnott/PAI-Reports
